Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . LOS ANGELES – New Los Angeles Lakers forward Ziaire Williams missed his first game of the season during the team’s 103-87 win against the LA Clippers on Wednesday due to a left foot injury. Ahead of the game, Lakers head coach JJ Redick acknowledged that the injury wasn’t expected to be anything serious and that it was more precautionary amid the rigid schedule. But in the two games the Lakers played prior to him being sidelined, Ziaire Williams had come under scrutiny by the NBA for perceived flopping . Williams was retroactively fined after the Lakers defeated the Utah Jazz last Sunday due to flopping. And then in the loss to the Portland Trail Blazers on Monday, he was hit with a technical foul by the officials for what they deemed flopping as well. Speaking to reporters after the loss to the Blazers, Williams was in disbelief over a lack of communication as to what the referees were considering flopping. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “If a dude is pushing off me, my body is naturally gonna waiver back. I don’t know. I don’t think I flopped but I don’t know. I don’t know. I really can’t answer that,” Williams had said during his postgame press conference. “They’ve just been calling it. I haven’t heard anything from anyone. Like I said, I don’t think I’m flopping. If I was flopping, I’d be on the floor. It is what it is, there’s nothing I can do about it now.” While Williams has been the one Lakers player singled out in that regard as of late, during the Blazers game, Ja Morant was also hit with a technical foul for perceived flopping. Following the game, he too was not given an explanation by the officials as to why he was called for a flopping technical, as per Law Murray of The Athletic. For Lakers head coach JJ Redick, he expressed the same sentiment as Williams in that sometimes players’ bodies make a natural motion when getting hit, and that doesn’t necessarily mean they’re trying to embellish anything. He also defended his player from the previous game against the Jazz after the fine. “They’re looking for theatrical things,” Redick said during his postgame press conference after the loss to the Blazers. “I also think Ziaire, his body naturally moves a certain way. I’ll have to rewatch, but I didn’t think the one the other night was a flop. That’s just the way his body naturally moves.” With that aside, Williams has made a strong impact in his first season with the Lakers . item.title: Every player from Arizona to play for the Golden State Warriors - Kevin Knox
item.description: The Golden State Warriors have signed, drafted, and traded for players from nearly every U.S. state and many countries around the world. From Alaska to Wyoming and Austria to Zaire, the Warriors have a strong history of seeking out talent necessary for NBA success. Since their beginnings in the Basketball Association of America (a precursor to the NBA) when they got their start as the team representing Philadelphia before they made their move to the West Coast, the organization has consistently pursued talent from a broad range of sources. For this installment of our series taking stock of the birthplace of every Golden State player to suit up for the franchise, let's take a look at every player from Arizona who has played for the Warriors. Our focus in this article is Kevin Knox. An alum of Kentucky, he was picked up with the ninth overall selection of the 2018 NBA Draft by the New York Knicks. The Phoenix, Arizona native played the first 4 seasons of his pro career with New York. He also played for the Atlanta Hawks, Detroit Pistons , Portland Trail Blazers , and Detroit again before he signed with the Dubs in 2024 for the final season of his NBA career. During his time suiting up for the Warriors, Knox put up 3.3 points and 1.2 rebounds per game. All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. item.title: Blu Cru Pramac Yamaha Announces 2027 Moto2 Team
item.description: Photos by Yamaha and Rob Gray (Polarity Photo). Yamaha has locked in its Moto2 line-up for 2027, signing Moto3 standout Álvaro Carpe to join the returning Alberto Ferrández on the BLU CRU Pramac Yamaha Moto2 Team. Both riders are 19 and represent Yamaha's ongoing push to funnel young talent up through the categories via its BLU CRU project. Ferrandez is currently in his first full Moto2 season, partnering with Izan Guevara with the Pramac Yamaha team. Facing a new category and several circuits he'd never seen before, his rookie year presented a steep learning curve, with Ferrández currently sitting 21st overall. For his second season, Yamaha expects him to take a big step forward, with Team Director Gino Borsoi setting a clear benchmark for Ferrandez to "establish himself consistently inside the top ten from the beginning of the championship." Carpe arrives from Moto3, where he spent the past two seasons with the Red Bull KTM Ajo team. Carpe finished fourth overall as a rookie in 2025, and finds himself in the same position this season. The team is tempering expectations for his first year in the intermediate category, with Borsoi hoping to see him "start translating his potential into encouraging results from the middle of the season onwards." Carpe will be taking over the seat currently occupied by Izan Guevara, who currently sits second in the Moto2 standings, trailing Manuel González by just 5.5 points, with five rounds remaining. Guevara is set to move up to Pramac Yamaha's MotoGP team in 2027. Guevara sets an example for Carpe's and Ferrández's path, progressing each year from a 22nd place finish in 2023 to fighting for the title this season. Become a Motorcycle.com insider. item.title: Columbus Blue Jackets come up short against Carolina Hurricanes
item.description: They finished strong in a road matchup against the reigning Stanley Cup champions, but the Blue Jackets couldn't overcome a three-goal deficit in a 3-2 loss to the Carolina Hurricanes on Oct. 29 in Raleigh, North Carolina. More: Cam Talbot continues to shine in Columbus Blue Jackets' OT win Denton Mateychuk and Kent Johnson scored goals 2:54 apart to pull the Blue Jackets (5-6-0) within 3-2 in the third period, but Mark Jankowski's goal for Carolina 16 seconds into the period was the difference. Hurricanes goalie Pyotr Kochetkov (24 saves) didn't allow another goal despite the Jackets pushing late with their net empty for a 6-on-5 advantage. "If you can have your building blocks off that, pressuring pucks and being in their face, it's hard to play against," Mateychuk said. "That's one of the best teams at it, and I feel like we gave them a bit of their own medicine in the third there. That's what they're used to doing to teams, and that's a glimpse of what we want to do for a full 60 [minutes]." Mateychuk cut it to 3-1 at 6:56 of the third to extend his goal streak to three straight games and Johnson followed by capping a power play at 9:50 for his seventh goal of the season. There just wasn't a tying goal in the cards for the Blue Jackets, who got 24 saves from goalie Jet Greaves in his first game since taking the loss Oct. 20 against the Toronto Maple Leafs . Jordan Martinook and Logan Stankoven scored the first two goals for the Hurricanes (11-2-2), who've won four of their past five games and sit comfortably atop the Metropolitan Division with 24 points and a cushion of eight points over the New Jersey Devils in second. The Blue Jackets will wrap up their first multi-game road trip of the season Oct. 31 in Dallas. item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Luka Doncic cleared for injury return in Warriors clash appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After being sidelined against the LA Clippers due to a back issue , Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic was off the team’s injury report ahead of their upcoming game on the road against the Golden State Warriors on Friday. Prior to Wednesday’s win against the Clippers, Lakers head coach JJ Redick acknowledged that Doncic’s status was nothing overly concerning, just precautionary as the team heads into a stretch of five games in seven nights. In addition to Luka Doncic, the Lakers might get forward Ziaire Williams back from injury as he was listed as questionable against the Warriors. Williams also was ruled out against the Clippers in similar precaution. The sixth-year wing signed with the Lakers in the offseason via free agency, and has been among the team’s most consistent players to this point as a starting forward. With Doncic back in the lineup, however, the on-court antics are certainly going to draw headlines as much, if not more, than the actual basketball. During the Lakers’ season opening win against the Warriors back on Oct. 21, Doncic was engaged in a trash-talking battle with Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg . Doncic got the better of that matchup, which included burying a half-court bomb to beat the halftime buzzer. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) After the game, both players acknowledged the chatter throughout the game, but Lendeborg took it a step further, proclaiming he had lost respect for Doncic due to his perceived complaining to the officials. Lendeborg was hit with a technical foul during the game, with teammate Draymond Green coming to his defense about. For the Lakers, the return of their star player is a much welcome development. The Slovenian native has gotten off to a blistering start to the season, and is among the early MVP candidates. He dropped a season-high 52 points last Sunday to help the Lakers grab a come-from-behind win against the Utah Jazz, and he followed that up with a 41-point effort despite a loss to the Portland Trail Blazers. Across the first four games of the season, Doncic is averaging a league-leading 36.0 points, 6.8 rebounds, 8.3 assists and 1.3 steals with splits of 48.4 percent shooting from the field, 39.6 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 87.5 percent shooting from the free-throw line. item.title: Lexington can't overcome slow start, falls in Division III district final
item.description: LEXINGTON — The Lexington Lady Lex found out the hard way the importance of starting soccer games off the right way. In their 2-1 Division III district championship loss to Elida on Thursday, Oct. 29, Lady Lex experienced a slow start and took a little too long to get things going. The loss ended their season with a 13-4-3 record. “I felt like we played with a lot of nerves,” Lexington coach Buck Morton said. “We never got the ball down to our feet. We knew that this would be a different level of game just from watching them on film and seeing that they moved more athletically and played with physicality. We knew it would be a tough game, but we had to play through not great touches.” KEEP UP WITH THE POSTSEASON: 2026 fall sports postseason tracker | Clear Fork wins girls soccer program's 10th district title Elida scored the opening goal off of a corner kick with 27:06 remaining in the first half and the score stood 1-0 into halftime. Lexington sophomore Jersie Palmer evened things up with 30:21 remaining when she rebounded a Morgan Harrod shot that drilled the post and bounced perfectly back to Palmer, who finished the goal. Lady Lex saw two more shots go off the cross bar and one more off the post as they were literally inches away from taking the lead multiple times. “We gave up a really soft goal on the cross. Any number of girls could have redirected that, but those things happen,” Morton said. “When we settled in and did what we have done all year long as a second-half team, we came back and had three really close calls on potential goals.” Elida took the lead for good with 18:22 remaining when Lexington was called for a late foul in the box. Lexie Good drilled the penalty kick to the upper 90 and gave Elida the lead and eventually the win. “I just didn’t agree with the call,” Morton said. “The ball was clearly away and nothing like that was called all night long and it was awarded with a PK. I didn’t agree with that at all. We came down and the girl basically catches the ball at the end of the game, and we had almost the same thing happen on our end and the reason for no call was because the ball was away. We already set that standard, so I will have to watch it again and maybe I’ll see it differently. “I am not putting the blame there. After a difficult start to the 2026 NFL season , injuries and consecutive losses have raised questions about the team’s ability to turn things around. With the possibility of an early first-round selection becoming more realistic, Roseman could have an opportunity to address one of the Eagles roster’s biggest needs in the 2027 NFL Draft. In the latest ClutchPoints 2027 NFL Mock Draft, Philadelphia selects South Carolina EDGE Dylan Stewart, a prospect who could provide a significant boost to its pass rush. His potential is undeniable, but concerns about his decision-making on and off the field could cause him to slide down the first round. Stewart’s upside makes him an appealing option, particularly if he remains available later than expected. The projected move also brings back memories of the 2023 NFL Draft , when Roseman traded up to select Jalen Carter despite concerns surrounding the defensive tackle’s pre-draft situation. Carter eventually became a cornerstone of Philadelphia’s defense, making that gamble worthwhile. Roseman has already shown that he is willing to take this kind of gamble when the talent is too good to pass up. It marks the first time this season that the Panthers recovered the opening kickoff. Plus also becomes the first fumble recovery by the Panthers’ special teams unit this season. Carolina and quarterback Bryce Young were handed a very short field to work with. Coach Dave Canales kept things simple in that sequence, trusting the ground attack with three running plays. item.description: Left: The San Francisco Giants' Madison Bumgarner and Buster Posey embrace after winning Game 7 of the 2014 World Series in Kansas City. Center: Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry watches the Cleveland Cavaliers celebrate after Game 7 of the 2016 NBA Finals at Oracle Arena. Right: The San Jose Sharks' Tomas Hertl leaps with joy after scoring a goal against the Colorado Avalanche in Game 7 of the 2019 Western Conference second round. (Scott Strazzante/S.F. Chronicle, Carlos Avila Gonzalez/S.F. Chronicle, Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) One compelling reason the words "Game 7" stir the sports fan's soul: It seldom happens. Only six times in Bay Area history has a local franchise played in Game 7 with the championship at stake. And only three times has that captivating, tension-filled, winner-take-all event taken place here: Giants-Yankees in the 1962 World Series, A's-Mets in the 1973 World Series and Warriors-Cavaliers in the 2016 NBA Finals. Now we have a fourth entry. Saturday's Game 7 of the WNBA Finals at Chase Center, featuring the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream, counts as a milestone on multiple levels. It also will mark the first time a WNBA postseason series has reached Game 7 - the league adopted a best-of-seven Finals format last year, when Las Vegas swept Phoenix. The previous year, in 2024, New York and Minnesota went the distance in their best-of-five Finals (the Liberty won 67-62 in Game 5). Any decisive game brings sporting theater, but Game 7s carry extra cachet - as the culmination of a long series, with sustained drama and wild momentum swings. That's exactly how this Valkyries-Dream duel has unfolded. Atlanta seemed in control after taking a 2-1 lead … and then Golden State stormed back to move ahead 3-2 … and then the Dream averted elimination with Thursday's emphatic victory. So now the series moves onto the grandest stage of all. Bay Area Game 7 history Saturday's showdown between the Valkyries and Atlanta Dream will be the 32nd time a Bay Area franchise has played in Game 7 of a postseason series - and only the seventh time it's happened with a championship at stake. The Detroit Red Wings have had a difficult season to this point and they find themselves tied for the bottom spot in the Atlantic Division of the Eastern Conference. In addition to trying to find a winning formula, they have had to deal with the trade demand of Dylan Larkin , their former captain. "I got to give Dylan a lot of credit. He went out and played hard for us. Dylan's been here for 12 years. In terms of sitting out, I can't put a timeline on it. With the teams on his list a trade is difficult." pic.twitter.com/NCgPsiZnhY — BucciOT.Com (@Buccigross) October 29, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) After making his demand public, Larkin played multiple games for the Red Wings before he let them know that he was not reporting to practice. As a result, the Red Wings have suspended Larkin without pay. “Dylan Larkin has informed us that he will no longer play for the Detroit Red Wings,” interim GM Shawn Horcoff said in a statement. “We are disappointed by his decision, particularly given his obligations to the organization and his teammates. We have therefore suspended Dylan without pay.” They are still trying to trade him, but Larkin has a list of just 10 teams that are on his accepted trade list. According to Horcoff, the limited number of teams on Larkin’s trade list makes it more difficult for t he Red Wings to make an acceptable trade . Horcoff has said on multiple occasions that the Red Wings would only make a deal that is beneficial to the team. Horcoff said he appreciated the effort that Larkin demonstrated in the 10 games that he has played this season for Detroit. Larkin had 2 goals and 4 assists in those games. Alex DeBrincat leads the team in scoring with 6 goals and 7 assists in 12 games. Veteran forwards Lucas Raymond and Viktor Arvidsson are right behind DeBrincat with 11 and 10 points, respectively.
